page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-480GB-2xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor, providing 24 physical cores and 24 vCPUs at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 480.0 GB of system memory, translating to 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs delivering a combined 160 GB of VRAM. Notably, this configuration does not include local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be attached.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory and decompression capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier result in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.63 GB/sec, alongside a strong multi-threaded decompression rate of 355.23 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is also strong, reaching 4086.55 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 290.6 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In LLM inference tests using a small 135M model, the server demonstrated top-tier performance, processing 10457.59 tokens/sec for prompts and generating 366.07 tokens/sec. CPU-bound benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core (52357.03) and PassMark CPU (55980.84), fall into the average to strong ranges, which may reflect the shared CPU allocation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high density of GPU resources and system memory relative to its vCPU count, making it a specialized option for workloads that rely heavily on GPU acceleration rather than dedicated host CPU cycles. The inclusion of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) further enhances its mathematical processing efficiency. This hardware profile is suited for large language model inference, deep learning training, data science pipelines, and database operations that can leverage GPU acceleration and large memory footprints, though users must account for the lack of built-in local storage.
